title: About the halcyon days what they meant
html_source:
A (past) period of idyllic calm, peace, and happiness; often nostalgic.

The phrase derives from the mythological Alcyone, daughter of wind god Aeolus. When her husband died in a shipwreck, Alcyone threw herself into the sea and the pitying gods transformed both her and her husband Ceyx into halcyon birds (kingfishers). When she made her nest on the beach, waves threatened to destroy it. Aeolus restrained the winds, providing seven days of calm each year so she could lay her eggs. These became known as the “halcyon days,” when storms do not occur.
